pages.title: Introduction
pages.content:
## Welcome to Kura

Every long-time player knows the problem: ten chests, three barrels and no idea where the iron went. Kura (Japanese for "storehouse") fixes that. It joins your chests into one network, so a single terminal shows everything you own, with search and sorting. No mods needed, it all works in the normal game.

### What you will do

* **Connect.** Run an Inventory Cable beside your chests. A cable joins whatever it touches, and so does every container touching those - that is the whole rule.
* **Find and fetch.** Open a Storage Terminal, search for an item and take it out. Put things back by clicking them in.
* **Craft from storage.** The Crafting Terminal uses what is in your network and refills its grid after each craft.
* **Reach it from anywhere.** Wireless terminals open your network from across the base, or even from another world with the advanced version.
* **Automate.** Hoppers, filters and level emitters keep machines supplied. They also work with Steamworks belts and arms.

### How the pages are organised

**Parts** explains every block you can place, **Tools** the items you carry (filters, configurator, wireless terminals, Paint Kit). **Recipes** shows how to craft them and **Automation** covers hoppers and redstone. Every part and tool has its own page.

### Good to know first

* Sake casks from Sakagura are never used as storage, so your drinks keep ageing.
* Furnaces, hoppers and brewing stands are not storage either.
* Kura talks to **/zukan**: from a Crafting Terminal you can look up a recipe and fill the grid from your network.

### Start here

1. Read [Kura Storage](/wiki?page=kura) for the one-minute explanation.
2. Look at [Parts](/wiki?page=kura-parts) and craft your first cable and terminal.
3. Come back to [Automation](/wiki?page=kura-automation) when the storage room is working.

pages.title: Kura Storage
pages.content:
## Kura - one terminal for all your chests

Kura joins your chests into one storage network. A **Storage Terminal** then shows every item in every connected chest on one screen, with search and sorting. Take things out, put things in, craft straight from storage, and reach it from across your base with a wireless terminal. You only need the normal game - no mods.

### How it works in one minute

There is **one rule: a cable joins whatever it touches.**

1. **Run an Inventory Cable** along your chests, barrels or shulker boxes. Every container a cable touches joins the network - and so does every container touching those.
2. **Place a Storage Terminal** against the cable (or against any chest in the network).
3. **Right-click the terminal.** Every item in the network is listed with its total amount.
4. **Click** an item to take a stack, **right-click** for half, **shift-click** to send it to your inventory. Click with an item on your cursor (or shift-click in your own inventory) to store it.

That is the whole system: no heart block to plan around, nothing to aim. Cables carry the network as far as you need them. Want them out of sight? The **Framed Inventory Cable** is a full-block cable that can be painted to look like the wall it runs through.

### Pages

* [Parts](/wiki?page=kura-parts) - cables, terminals, hopper, emitter, interface, crate, cabinet
* [Tools](/wiki?page=kura-tools) - filters, Inventory Configurator, wireless terminals, Paint Kit
* [Recipes](/wiki?page=kura-recipes) - how to craft every part
* [Automation](/wiki?page=kura-automation) - hoppers, Steamworks belts and arms, redstone

### Search tips

| Type | Finds |
|---|---|
| iron | items with "iron" in the name |
| #logs | every item in a group (tag), e.g. all logs |
| @kitchen | every item of one plugin (kitchen, steamworks, sakagura...) |

Type **/kura** in game for a short help and a link back here.

pages.title: Parts
pages.content:
## Parts

Most parts are placed like blocks. **Taking one off:** sneak + right-click it with an **empty hand** (one click, any game mode), or punch it three times (one in creative). The Interface and Open Crate are real barrels and break like any barrel. To place a part against a chest, **sneak** while placing - otherwise the chest just opens.

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Inventory Cable** | The network. Touches a chest, barrel or shulker box and that container is in; touches another cable and the two become one network. Any cable makes a network on its own - there is no "heart" block to plan around. |
| **Framed Inventory Cable** | The same cable that fills the whole block, so it can run through a wall. Can be painted to look like any solid block. |
| **Storage Terminal** | Shows and handles every item in the network. Place it against a cable or against any chest of the network. On a lone chest (no cable anywhere) it shows just that chest. |
| **Crafting Terminal** | A Storage Terminal with a 3x3 crafting grid. After each craft the grid **refills itself** from the network, so you can keep clicking. **Shift-click** the result to craft a whole stack. |
| **Inventory Hopper** | Moves items from the block behind it to the block in front, 8 at a time. Either side can be a whole network, a chest, or an Open Crate. Right-click to set a filter. |
| **Level Emitter** | Gives a redstone signal when the network holds more (or less) than a set amount of one item. Right-click to set the item and amount. |
| **Inventory Interface** | A barrel. **Import**: everything put in goes into the network. **Export**: it is kept stocked with one stack of each item in its filter. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand for settings. |
| **Open Crate** | A barrel that drops everything put into it on the ground in front. Sneak while placing to make it drop downwards. |
| **Filing Cabinet** | Holds up to 256 items of **one kind** in all variants - perfect for enchanted books, potions or maps. Keeps its contents when broken. Works as part of a network too. |


* [Old parts (0.1.11 and earlier)](/wiki?page=kura-parts-old-parts-0-1-11-and)
* [Good to know](/wiki?page=kura-parts-good-to-know)

pages.title: Old parts (0.1.11 and earlier)
pages.content:
Three parts used to do what a single cable does now. They can no longer be crafted, but **everything already placed keeps working** - each one behaves as a cable, keeps its look and its name:

| Part | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Inventory Connector** | The heart of a network; without one nothing joined. | Behaves as a cable. |
| **Inventory Trim** | Bridged a gap between chests; stores nothing; could be painted. | Behaves as a cable (still paintable). |
| **Cable Connector** | The piece at the end of a cable, aimed at the chest it attached. | Behaves as a cable: it joins every side, no aiming needed. |

Back to [Parts](/wiki?page=kura-parts)

pages.title: Good to know
pages.content:
* Furnaces, hoppers and brewing stands are never used as storage, and neither are Sakagura sake casks (your drinks keep ageing).
* Right-click a cable to see how big its network is - its blocks light up for a few seconds.
* A very big network (over 4096 blocks) stops growing; the terminal tells you when that happens.

Back to [Parts](/wiki?page=kura-parts)

pages.title: Tools
pages.content:
## Tools


* [Filters](/wiki?page=kura-tools-filters)
* [Inventory Configurator](/wiki?page=kura-tools-inventory-configurator)
* [Wireless terminals](/wiki?page=kura-tools-wireless-terminals)
* [Paint Kit](/wiki?page=kura-tools-paint-kit)

pages.title: Filters
pages.content:
Filters go into a **filter slot** (Inventory Configurator, Inventory Hopper, Inventory Interface). You can also put any normal item in a filter slot: then only that item passes.

| Filter | How to set it up |
|---|---|
| **Item Filter** | Right-click it, then click slots with items to add them. Switch between "allow only these" and "block these", and between "any item of this kind" and "exact match" (names, enchantments). |
| **Tag Filter** | Right-click it, put an item in the top row, then click below it to pick one of its groups - e.g. all logs, all wool, all flowers. |
| **Polymorphic Filter** | Nothing to set: only lets in items the container already holds. Great for keeping each chest for the items it already has. |

Back to [Tools](/wiki?page=kura-tools)

pages.title: Inventory Configurator
pages.content:
Right-click a chest that is part of a network to change how the network uses it:

* **Priority** (lowest to highest): higher priority chests fill first and are emptied last.
* **Filter**: only matching items go in.
* **Left out of networks**: the network skips this chest completely.
* **Keep last item**: leaves one item in each slot, so the slot stays reserved for that item.
* **Show network**: lights up every block of the network.

Right-click a hopper, emitter or interface with it to open its settings.

Back to [Tools](/wiki?page=kura-tools)

pages.title: Wireless terminals
pages.content:
* **Wireless Terminal** - right-click while looking at a terminal up to 16 blocks away.
* **Advanced Wireless Terminal** - sneak + right-click a terminal to bind it, then right-click anywhere within 64 blocks. A **beacon** within 8 blocks of the terminal makes it reachable from anywhere in the same world (level 1-3) or from any world (level 4).

Back to [Tools](/wiki?page=kura-tools)

pages.title: Paint Kit
pages.content:
Right-click any full block to pick its look, then right-click a Framed Cable (or an old Inventory Trim) to give it that look. Sneak + right-click to clear it. The kit wears out after 64 uses.

Back to [Tools](/wiki?page=kura-tools)

pages.title: Recipes
pages.content:
## Recipes

Shaped recipes are shown as rows (top / middle / bottom); a dot is an empty slot. Shapeless recipes can be put in any order.

| Item | Recipe |
|---|---|
| Storage Terminal | C G C / R Q R / C C C - C copper ingot, G glass pane, R redstone, Q comparator |
| Crafting Terminal | Storage Terminal + crafting table + gold ingot |
| Inventory Cable (6) | C R C - copper ingot, redstone, copper ingot |
| Framed Inventory Cable | Inventory Cable + 2 sticks |
| Inventory Hopper | Hopper + copper ingot + redstone |
| Level Emitter | Comparator + redstone torch + copper ingot |
| Inventory Interface | Barrel + 2 copper ingots + redstone |
| Open Crate | Barrel + iron bars |
| Filing Cabinet | I P I / P H P / I P I - I iron ingot, P paper, H chest |
| Wireless Terminal | Storage Terminal + ender pearl + gold ingot + redstone |
| Advanced Wireless Terminal | Wireless Terminal + eye of ender + diamond + gold ingot |
| Item Filter (2) | 2 paper + copper ingot |
| Tag Filter | Item Filter + book |
| Polymorphic Filter | Item Filter + chest |
| Inventory Configurator | Stick + copper ingot + redstone + glass pane |
| Paint Kit | Brush + red dye + green dye + blue dye |

**Recipes on the website**

Since 0.1.11 the **Inventory Cable** is the only joiner: the Inventory Connector, Inventory Trim and Cable Connector
are no longer crafted - what is already placed on the server keeps working as a cable.

All Steamworks, Kitchen and Kura recipes are also listed on the website: **Play > Recipes**. That page has a search and a type filter, and a short guide to Zukan.

pages.title: Automation
pages.content:
## Automation

Kura works with vanilla hoppers and with **Steamworks** machines, because its Inventory Interface and Open Crate are real barrels.


* [Getting items in](/wiki?page=kura-automation-getting-items-in)
* [Getting items out](/wiki?page=kura-automation-getting-items-out)
* [Redstone](/wiki?page=kura-automation-redstone)
* [Tips](/wiki?page=kura-automation-tips)

pages.title: Getting items in
pages.content:
* **Vanilla hopper or Steamworks conveyor belt into an Inventory Interface** (import mode): everything that arrives is stored in the network. A farm can feed your storage directly.
* **Steamworks Karakuri Arm**: let it DROP items into an Interface.
* **Inventory Hopper** pointing from a farm chest into any network chest: moves the farm's output into storage.

Back to [Automation](/wiki?page=kura-automation)

pages.title: Getting items out
pages.content:
* **Inventory Interface in export mode**: put an Item Filter with what you need in it (for example coal and iron). The barrel is kept topped up with one stack of each, so hoppers, belts and arms can take from it - for example to feed a Steamworks boiler or millstone.
* **Inventory Hopper from the network into an Open Crate**: the items fall out in front of the crate, onto a conveyor belt or into a water stream.

Back to [Automation](/wiki?page=kura-automation)

pages.title: Redstone
pages.content:
* A **Level Emitter** turns on when the network holds more (or less) than an amount of one item. Use it to switch a farm off when storage is full, or to start a machine when supplies run low.

Back to [Automation](/wiki?page=kura-automation)

pages.title: Tips
pages.content:
* Give your "dump" chests the **lowest priority** and your sorted chests a filter with **higher priority** (Inventory Configurator). Items then land in the sorted chests first.
* A **Polymorphic Filter** on a chest keeps it for the items already in it.

Back to [Automation](/wiki?page=kura-automation)

pages.title: Copper Golem Couriers
pages.content:
## Copper Golem Couriers

A copper golem can work as a courier for your storage network: it fetches items from supply points and carries them into the network.


* [Set it up](/wiki?page=kura-couriers-set-it-up)
* [What it fetches](/wiki?page=kura-couriers-what-it-fetches)
* [Good to know](/wiki?page=kura-couriers-good-to-know)

pages.title: Set it up
pages.content:
1. Place an **Inventory Interface** that is connected to your network.
2. Stand next to a copper golem that is within 12 blocks of the interface.
3. Right-click the golem with an **Inventory Configurator**. The golem is bound to the nearest interface.
4. Right-click it again with the configurator to set it free.

Back to [Copper Golem Couriers](/wiki?page=kura-couriers)

pages.title: What it fetches
pages.content:
* Items from **copper chests** around the interface.
* With Steamworks installed: the chests and barrels that **machines deliver into** - under a steam hammer, under or beside a kettle or millstone, and at the end of a conveyor belt.

It never empties the network itself, and it only works while you are online and allowed to build at the supply point.

Back to [Copper Golem Couriers](/wiki?page=kura-couriers)

pages.title: Good to know
pages.content:
* The golem takes one stack at a time and walks it to the interface.
* If the network is full, it puts the rest down instead of standing around.
* A golem that is not bound keeps behaving like a normal copper golem.
* The radius can be changed in the Kura config (`couriers.radius`, 4-24 blocks).

Back to [Copper Golem Couriers](/wiki?page=kura-couriers)
